BIDEX.TAGLINE: Pokédex and competitive tools for mobile and web
BIDEX.SUMMARY: Browse the Pokédex, create builds and teams, and share them with the community. The app works offline and syncs your data across devices. Developed by me from start to finish.

BIDEX_CASE.SUBTITLE: How BiDex works under the hood
BIDEX_CASE.INTRO: BiDex is a Pokédex with competitive tools that I built on my own. This page explains what the app does and the technical decisions behind it. The mobile version is the core of the project.

OVERVIEW.TITLE: Overview
OVERVIEW.TEXT: The app reads almost everything from local databases and only uses the network to sync. There are two main data flows:
OVERVIEW.NOTE: The Pokédex ships inside the app and is updated separately, so it barely needs to query the server.

FEATURES.TITLE: What the app does
FEATURES.POKEDEX: Searchable, filterable list including forms and variants.
FEATURES.DETAIL: Information, stats, moves and type effectiveness.
FEATURES.TEAMS: Editor for teams of 6 with item, ability, nature and stats.
FEATURES.COVERAGE: Analyses the team's weaknesses, resistances and immunities.
FEATURES.EXPLORE: Community space to search, share and vote on builds and teams.
FEATURES.TYPECALC: Multipliers for a combination of up to two types.
FEATURES.GAMEDEX: Catch tracking by game and by region.
FEATURES.SHARE: Generates a ready-to-send image of a team or build.
FEATURES.MYBOX: All your builds and teams, with search and filters.
FEATURES.MOVES: Catalogue with power, accuracy, PP, priority and filters.
FEATURES.ABILITIES: Every ability with its generation and description.
FEATURES.ITEMS: Item catalogue with search and filters.
FEATURES.COMPARE: Puts the stats of two Pokémon side by side.
FEATURES.PROFILE: Your details, stats, builds, teams and friend code.
FEATURES.AVATAR: Choose a Pokémon, then one of its expressions.

SYNC.TITLE: Offline-first sync
SYNC.PROBLEM: Players should be able to edit their builds and teams without coverage, without losing anything and without waiting for the server.
SYNC.SOLUTION: Every write goes to SQLite first. The same transaction adds an entry to a sync queue, which is sent later in the background.
SYNC.P1: IDs are client-generated UUIDs, so nothing needs remapping on upload.
SYNC.P2: The queue merges operations: several edits are sent as one, and creating then deleting before upload cancels out.
SYNC.P3: A priority guarantees dependency order: EV sets, then builds, then teams.
SYNC.P4: Temporary failures are retried with exponential backoff, up to five times.
SYNC.P5: When sending, the engine re-reads the current row, so the latest version is always uploaded.
SYNC.P6: Downloads are incremental. Conflicts are resolved with last-write-wins, using the server timestamp.
SYNC.RESULT: The app responds instantly with or without a connection, and changes reach the server on their own once it returns.

CONTENT.TITLE: Updating the Pokédex without an app release
CONTENT.PROBLEM: Data changes often, and going through Google Play for every fix would be slow. Querying it remotely would leave offline users without a Pokédex.
CONTENT.SOLUTION: A script exports the data to one SQLite file per language and publishes them to Cloudflare R2. The app detects the new version on startup and downloads it.
CONTENT.P1: Denormalised views prepare the data, and a script generates the databases with their indexes.
CONTENT.P2: A latest.json file publishes the version, sizes and SHA-256 hashes.
CONTENT.P3: Each version states the minimum app version, protecting older installs.
CONTENT.P4: The whole database is replaced, with no migrations. Only additive changes are allowed, because installed apps keep reading the same schema.
CONTENT.P5: If the download fails or the hash does not match, the app keeps the data it already had.
CONTENT.RESULT: I can publish content in minutes with no store review, and the Pokédex always works offline.

IMAGES.TITLE: Images and offline pack
IMAGES.PROBLEM: There are over 3,500 images. Bundling them all would make the app huge, but without them the offline experience suffers.
IMAGES.SOLUTION: A manifest with each image's SHA-1 hash means only what changed is downloaded, and users choose whether they want the full pack.
IMAGES.P1: The deploy script compares hashes and uploads only new or modified files to R2.
IMAGES.P2: The app downloads the pack with up to 15 concurrent downloads and retries.
IMAGES.P3: Each image is looked up in memory first, then on disk and finally on the network.
IMAGES.P4: Whatever is viewed online is saved in the background, so the cache grows with use.
IMAGES.P5: Images use WebP, with sprites averaging around 20 KB.
IMAGES.RESULT: The app stays light, and with the pack installed it works offline with all its images.

ACCOUNTS.TITLE: Accounts and guest mode
ACCOUNTS.PROBLEM: Forcing sign-up puts off people who only want to look something up, yet those who do register should not lose what they created.
ACCOUNTS.SOLUTION: The whole app works in guest mode. On sign-in, local data is migrated to the account and synced.
ACCOUNTS.P1: As a guest, changes are saved and queued as usual, but are not sent until there is an account.
ACCOUNTS.P2: Migration runs in one transaction: it assigns new IDs, updates relations and queues everything in order.
ACCOUNTS.P3: Deletions are soft, so other devices find out about them.
ACCOUNTS.RESULT: There are no barriers to using it, and signing up does not mean starting over.

SHARING.TITLE: Importing builds and teams
SHARING.PROBLEM: Players swap teams all the time. An imported copy cannot depend on or clash with the original, because each user must be able to edit and sync it independently.
SHARING.SOLUTION: There are two import routes: BiDex codes and Pokémon Showdown text. Both produce an independent copy that enters the normal sync flow.
SHARING.P1: A BiDex code is resolved on the server: it is looked up as a team first and, if not found, as a build.
SHARING.P2: Everything is cloned with new UUIDs generated on the phone: the team, each build and their EV sets.
SHARING.P3: Relations are rewritten in the same transaction: slots, moves, stat points and EV values all point to the new IDs.
SHARING.P4: The copy starts private, with zero votes and no code of its own, even if the original was public.
SHARING.P5: Each entity is queued with its priority: EV sets, builds, then the team. The server therefore never receives a reference to something that does not exist yet.
SHARING.P6: Showdown uses names, not IDs. The parser resolves them against the English database, even when the app is in Spanish, and flags anything unrecognised before importing.
SHARING.RESULT: Once imported, the copy is yours: it can be edited offline and does not affect the original.

ENGINE.TITLE: Competitive engine
ENGINE.PROBLEM: The tools are only useful if they follow the game's rules, including those of the Champions format.
ENGINE.SOLUTION: Calculation logic is separated from the UI, and covers stat points, conversion and type coverage.
ENGINE.P1: Champions applies its own formulas and limits: 32 points per stat and 66 in total.
ENGINE.P2: Classic EVs are converted to stat points in two passes, sharing out the available total proportionally.
ENGINE.P3: Coverage combines types, Terastallization and abilities, with special cases such as Wonder Guard or Tera Shell.
ENGINE.RESULT: The analysis reflects the actual team, not just the type chart.

WEB.TITLE: Web version
WEB.TEXT: The web version is built with Angular and TypeScript on the same backend, so builds, teams and votes are shared. It adds public links to each build and profile, plus Showdown export. It has no offline mode, My Pokédex or share cards.

MESSAGES.TITLE: Messages and reports
MESSAGES.PROBLEM: Without a direct channel, I cannot tell users about news or learn about the errors they find.
MESSAGES.SOLUTION: A remote welcome message lets me reach them without an app release, and a built-in form brings me their reports.
MESSAGES.P1: Messages are defined in a JSON file hosted on the CDN, translated into each language.
MESSAGES.P2: The app filters by expiry, minimum version and language, and remembers dismissed messages.
MESSAGES.P3: With no connection it uses the last saved copy; if there is none, nothing is shown.
MESSAGES.P4: The report form separates bugs, suggestions and translations, and prefills details when signed in.
MESSAGES.P5: An Edge Function forwards each report to a private Discord channel.
MESSAGES.RESULT: I can announce changes straight away and get feedback in one place.

DEXSYNC.TITLE: My Pokédex sync
DEXSYNC.PROBLEM: Storing every catch in PostgreSQL would take up space and generate many writes for data only its owner uses.
DEXSYNC.SOLUTION: Progress lives in a local JSON file and syncs whole as a single file on Cloudflare R2, through a Worker.
DEXSYNC.P1: It works the same offline, because the local file is the reference.
DEXSYNC.P2: Changes upload when leaving the screen or minimising the app.
DEXSYNC.P3: Before downloading it checks only the date, with a 10-minute pause between checks.
DEXSYNC.P4: The file is replaced whole and the newest version wins, with no merging.
DEXSYNC.RESULT: Progress follows the user across devices without taking up database space.
